correctness.rationale: The prescribed nonintegral Cauchy kernel is exactly the Fourier coefficient of m_t(theta)=exp(i t(pi-theta)) for 0<theta<2pi, including the correct signed integer translations. Since a,b>0 the checkerboard l2 norm is equivalent to ordinary l2 and the Fourier extension is bounded. Parity-folding pairs theta and theta+pi, with metric W=[[u,v],[v,u]], u=(a+b)/2,v=(a-b)/2; the operator is a unimodular scalar times B_t=W^{1/2} diag(1,e^{-i pi t}) W^{-1/2}. Its |det|=1 and trace(B_t*B_t)=2+4 beta^2 sin^2(pi t/2), beta=|a-b|/(2 sqrt(ab)). Singular values s,s^-1 solve s-s^-1=2 beta |sin|, yielding the boxed exact norm for all real t. Because this matrix is constant over the entire Fourier fiber, an L2 function supported on its top singular vector yields actual nonzero maximizers; equality is fiberwise necessary. Equal weights/even integer t give isometries and all vectors extremize. Six independently recomputed fiber trace/singular-value identities passed; no finite Fourier quadrature was treated as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Finite exact computations diagnose bounded instances only; analytic derivation controls general quantifiers.

value.rationale: Periodic two-weight metrics are the first genuinely non-isometric example for a unitary fractional discrete-translation group. The exact all-real-parameter norm, sharp amplifying contrast, and attained equality subspaces quantify nonnormality/condition amplification, rather than merely repeating a known weighted boundedness estimate. The two-by-two folding reduction is elementary but gives a fully sharp, directly usable operator-norm profile and extremizers.
